# Results — Study 953 (Replicating the Convert) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The exercise: fit **CWB**'s
daily **total-return** excess-of-cash series to a **static long-only mix** of **SPY**
(large-cap equity), **QQQ** (the growth tilt convertible issuers actually carry) and
**LQD** (investment-grade credit), with the unspent weight in **BIL** (T-bills); fit
**in-sample only**, freeze the weights, and score the **out-of-sample** residual alpha
and the convexity claim. Daily total-return closes (`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True`).
Common CWB∩SPY∩QQQ∩LQD∩BIL window 2009-04-16 → 2026-06-30. As-of **2026-06-30** (the
partial current month is dropped) — data stamp as-of 2026-06-30.*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| CWB (fund), SPY / QQQ / LQD (replication kit), BIL (cash) | 2009-04-16 → 2026-06-30 | 4,328 | Fingerprint `5e5674563124` |

Cross-check: ICVT (a second convertible ETF, 2015-06-04 →) is cached too.

**Conventions.** One execution lag, and exactly one: the weights are estimated on data
**through 2017-12-31** and applied from **2018-01-02** onward; the month-end drift is
carried through the return of the first trading day of the new month and only traded back
to target at **that** day's close (the zero-lag alternative — a month-end-close rebalance —
moves the hold-out alpha by 5 bps/yr and the *t* by 0.02). Costs are **3 bps one-way ×
NAV** on traded turnover. All series are **total return** and every comparison is
**excess-of-cash vs excess-of-cash** (BIL's actual total return is the cash leg, so the
race credits the real path of short rates — 0% in 2009-2015, ~5% in 2023-2026).

**Proxies / assumptions (not tape), all swept below.** (a) The replica pays a **10 bps/yr**
blended fee drag — a stand-in for what a SPY/QQQ/LQD sleeve actually costs; swept 0-20.
(b) CWB's and ICVT's returns are already **net of their own expense ratios** (0.40% and
0.20% per the issuers) because the fee comes out of NAV daily — that number is quoted, not
measured here. (c) The 2017-12-31 in-sample boundary is a choice — swept across seven years
below. (d) The **SPY/QQQ/LQD kit is a judgement**, and a hindsight-flavoured one: we know
today that convertible issuers skew growth, and a richer kit mechanically shrinks the very
residual being measured. It is swept down to a single equity leg below rather than defended.

## The fitted replication (in-sample only, 2009-04-17 → 2017-12-29, n = 2,193)

| Leg | Weight |
|---|--:|
| SPY | 36.7% |
| QQQ | 20.2% |
| LQD | 5.8% |
| Cash (BIL) | 37.3% |

In-sample R² **0.703**, tracking error **5.68%/yr**, intercept **+1.12%/yr**. The fitted
convertible fund is, to a first approximation, **57% equity (two-thirds S&P, one-third
Nasdaq), 6% investment-grade credit and 37% cash** — an odd but revealing recipe: the
"bond" half of a convertible behaves far more like *cash plus an equity stub* than like
duration-bearing credit. The long-only budget constraint **never binds** — the
unconstrained OLS solution is already inside it (identical weights to three decimals), so
no leg goes short and **no borrow cost arises**.

## The hold-out — is the residual alpha distinguishable from zero?

| Window | n days | Residual alpha | HAC *t* | Tracking error | corr(fund, replica) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| In-sample 2009-04-17 → 2017-12-29 *(fitted here — not evidence)* | 2,193 | +1.28%/yr | +0.80 | 5.68%/yr | 0.838 |
| **Out-of-sample 2018-01-02 → 2026-06-30** | **2,134** | **+1.80%/yr** | **+0.58** | 8.30%/yr | 0.850 |

- **Block-bootstrap CI** (2,000 draws, 21-day blocks) on the out-of-sample alpha:
  **+1.80% [−4.47%, +7.55%]**, 71.4% of resamples positive. The interval is six percentage
  points wide in each direction and comfortably straddles zero.
- **Excess-of-cash Sharpe race** (both legs excess of BIL's own total return): fund
  **+0.662** vs replica **+0.725** — the frozen three-ETF mix *edges* the fund it was fitted
  to, on a hold-out it never saw. The gap (−0.063) is noise.
- **Risk:** fund vol 15.51% vs replica 11.69% (the replica holds 37% cash by construction);
  max drawdown fund **−32.24%** vs replica −19.46%, and **−25.25%** for a vol-matched
  replica. The wrapper carries more risk per unit of the same return.
- **Replication quality is good, not tight:** monthly R² **0.764**, monthly tracking error
  **7.85%/yr**. Three ETFs explain about three-quarters of CWB's month-to-month variation;
  the last quarter is genuinely idiosyncratic — and, as the crash months below show, it is
  not idiosyncratic in the investor's favour.

## The convexity claim (out-of-sample months, sorted by SPY excess return, n = 102)

The pitch is a *shape*, not a level: catch the rally, cushion the fall. Against its own
frozen replica, a convex wrapper should win in **both** tail terciles — a smile. *This is a
**description** of a realised payoff, not a tradable rule: the tercile breakpoints and the
up/down split are computed on the whole hold-out, so a month's bucket is known only in
arrears. Nothing downstream trades on it.*

| Tercile of SPY excess | Fund − replica (bps/month) | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| Bottom (worst months) | **−55.8** | −1.57 |
| Middle | +29.9 | — |
| Top (best months) | **+72.5** | +1.56 |

- **Smile (tails − middle): −21.6 bps/month, Welch *t* = −0.50.** The pattern is not a
  smile but a **straight line**: the fund adds in up months and gives it back in down
  months, one for one.
- **Up-capture vs replica 1.219, down-capture 1.215 — asymmetry +0.004.** CWB captures 22%
  more of its replica's gains *and* 22% more of its losses. That is **extra beta**, not
  convexity.
- **Treynor-Mazuy curvature** on the fund-minus-replica difference: γ = **+0.192**
  (HAC *t* = **+0.25**). Indistinguishable from a straight line.

## Robustness

| Cut | Window | n | Alpha | HAC *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Hold-out, early era | 2018-01-02 → 2021-12-31 | 1,008 | +4.68%/yr | +0.86 |
| Hold-out, late era | 2022-01-03 → 2026-06-30 | 1,126 | −0.78%/yr | −0.23 |
| Annual refit (expanding window, always forward) | 2014-01-02 → 2026-06-30 | 3,141 | +1.35%/yr | +0.61 |
| Unconstrained fit (shorts would pay 50 bps borrow; none appear) | 2018-01-02 → 2026-06-30 | 2,134 | +1.80%/yr | +0.58 |

The single fixed split is not doing the work: refitting the weights every year and always
applying them forward gives the same answer (+1.35%/yr, *t* = +0.61). What little residual
there is lives entirely in **2018-2021** — the SPAC-and-growth-issuance boom, when
convertible issuers were exactly the meme-adjacent names that ran — and it is gone in
2022-2026. The last fitted weights (through 2025) drift toward more credit and less cash:
SPY 34.5% / QQQ 24.2% / LQD 16.2% / cash 25.1%.

### Were the two judgement calls doing the work?

Both hindsight-flavoured choices — the QQQ leg and the 2017 boundary — are swept rather
than defended. Neither rescues the fund, and a *leaner* kit (which is the one a 2009
observer would have picked) leaves a **bigger** residual that is still nowhere near the bar:

| Replication kit | IS R² | Cash weight | OOS alpha | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY only | 0.685 | 42.8% | +3.01%/yr | +0.92 |
| SPY + LQD | 0.686 | 36.7% | +2.99%/yr | +0.94 |
| SPY + QQQ | 0.702 | 43.2% | +1.81%/yr | +0.57 |
| **SPY + QQQ + LQD** (headline) | **0.703** | **37.3%** | **+1.80%/yr** | **+0.58** |

| In-sample boundary | n OOS | OOS alpha | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2014-12-31 | 2,889 | +1.91%/yr | +0.79 |
| 2015-12-31 | 2,637 | +2.35%/yr | +0.90 |
| 2016-12-31 | 2,385 | +1.93%/yr | +0.69 |
| **2017-12-31** (headline) | **2,134** | **+1.80%/yr** | **+0.58** |
| 2018-12-31 | 1,883 | +1.83%/yr | +0.54 |
| 2019-12-31 | 1,631 | +1.82%/yr | +0.47 |
| 2020-12-31 | 1,378 | −2.72%/yr | −0.80 |

Across **eleven** specifications — four kits and seven boundaries — the largest |*t*| any
of them reaches is **0.94**, and one of them is *negative*. The blank is a property of the
fund, not of the specification.

## Cost and fee sensitivity

Turnover is trivial (static weights, monthly rebalance), so friction barely moves the
answer — and the replica's *own* fee drag flatters the fund, so charging it honestly makes
the residual *larger*, not smaller:

| One-way cost | Replica fee | Alpha | HAC *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| 0 bps | 0 bps/yr | +1.69%/yr | +0.54 |
| 3 bps | 10 bps/yr | +1.80%/yr | +0.58 |
| 10 bps | 20 bps/yr | +1.91%/yr | +0.62 |

Across the whole 4 × 3 grid the alpha moves by 22 bps/yr and the *t* by 0.08. **No cost
assumption can rescue or condemn this result** — it is a *t* below 1 whatever you charge.

## ICVT cross-check (a second convertible ETF, in-sample through 2020-12-31)

Fitted mix SPY 37.2% / QQQ 23.6% / LQD 24.5% / cash 14.7% (in-sample R² 0.568). Out-of-sample
2021-01-04 → 2026-06-30 (n = 1,378): residual alpha **−2.16%/yr**, HAC *t* = **−0.56** — zero
again, with the sign flipped. Up-capture **0.802** vs down-capture **0.871**: ICVT captures
*less* of the upside than of the downside, the opposite of convexity. Smile +21.1 bps
(*t* = +0.32).

## Where the "bond floor" actually was

The three worst out-of-sample months for the fund relative to its replica:

| Month | Fund (excess) | Replica (excess) | Shortfall |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2020-03 | **−13.28%** | −6.49% | **−6.79%** |
| 2021-03 | −4.03% | +1.92% | −5.95% |
| 2021-11 | −4.51% | +0.11% | −4.62% |

In the March-2020 crash the convertible fund lost **twice** what its own static equity-plus-
credit-plus-cash replica lost. Whatever the bond floor is worth in a prospectus, it was not
worth anything in the one month it was asked for.

## Synthetic control (machinery proof — never market evidence)

On a *planted* fund — a static mix plus a genuine 2%/yr alpha and a genuine delta ratchet
(equity exposure rising after rallies, falling after selloffs, which is exactly what a real
convertible does) — the harness recovers the true weights to within 6 pp and reports OOS
alpha **+5.02%/yr (*t* = +3.97)**, TM curvature **γ = +0.73 (*t* = +3.45)** and a smile of
**+26.7 bps/month**. On the null (the same fund with both effects switched off) across 8
seeds: alpha *t* mean **+0.03** (sd 0.87), |*t*| ≥ 2 in **0/8**; curvature *t* mean +0.01,
|*t*| ≥ 2 in **0/8**. The detector fires when there is something to find and stays quiet
when there is not — so the real-tape blank is a fact about convertible ETFs, not a broken
harness.

## Verdict

- **Signal — None.** The residual alpha of the most popular convertible ETF over a static
  SPY/QQQ/LQD/cash mix, on a genuine hold-out, is **+1.80%/yr with HAC *t* = +0.58** and a
  bootstrap CI of **[−4.47%, +7.55%]** — statistically indistinguishable from zero, and the
  desk's bar is |*t*| ≥ 2. It is +4.68%/yr in 2018-2021 and −0.78%/yr in 2022-2026, so it is
  not era-robust either; an annual refit gives the same *t* = +0.61; no kit and no boundary
  in an eleven-specification sweep gets |*t*| past **0.94**; the second fund (ICVT) gives
  **−2.16%/yr, *t* = −0.56**. The convexity claim fails separately and more cleanly:
  up-capture 1.219 versus down-capture 1.215 (asymmetry **+0.004**), a *negative* tail smile
  (−21.6 bps/month, *t* = −0.50) and a Treynor-Mazuy curvature of +0.19 (*t* = +0.25). What
  the wrapper delivers is **more beta**, symmetric in both directions — the one thing you do
  not need a convertible to buy. **Survivorship:** CWB and ICVT are two *surviving*,
  currently-listed funds; convertible vehicles that closed (and the closed-end funds that
  de-listed) are not in this tape, so if anything the sample is tilted toward the wrapper.
- **Tradability — Mirage.** There is nothing to bank in either direction. Long the fund:
  the residual is a coin flip that costs a certain 0.40%/yr in fees. Short the fund against
  the replica: the *t* is 0.58 and the monthly tracking error is **7.85%/yr**, so the
  "arbitrage" is a 2%/yr expectation inside an 8%/yr noise band — and the noise is skewed
  against you (−6.8% in a single month in March 2020). The honest read is not "sell CWB and
  buy the replica"; it is that **you are not buying a distinct asset class**. A 57/6/37
  equity/credit/cash sleeve is what you own, and the fee is the only thing about it you can
  predict.
